data.abstract: On-load voltage regulating transformers play a crucial role in power systems, not only connecting to the grid but also regulating reactive power and stabilizing loads. The on-load tap-changer (OLTC), as the key component of the on-load regulator, is the only movable part of the transformer, and its reliability is directly related to the safe and stable operation of the power grid. Therefore, timely identification of operational defects and rapid localization of mechanical faults in OLTCs through online monitoring is crucial for the operation and maintenance of transformers in the field. In this paper, firstly, the mechanism of on-load tap-changer contact faults is analyzed in depth, and on this basis, a diagnostic method for OLTC contact faults is proposed for the joint analysis of electric-vibrational signal features. Secondly, in order to extract high-quality fault features, the Ensemble Empirical Mode Decomposition (EEMD) algorithm is used to process the vibration signals and motor current signals to extract the fault features. Meanwhile, their envelope time-domain features are extracted by the Hilbert transform. Finally, the experimentally obtained electric-vibration joint signal features are utilized to deeply analyze the contact state of OLTC and evaluate its fault state.

data.abstract: With the continuous construction of power system in China, the safe and stable operation of power system has become a very important problem. The On-Load Tap Changer (OLTC), as the only movable part in power transformer, plays an important role in the stable operation of the transformer and even the whole power system. At present, the fault diagnosis of the OLTC based on the vibration signal has become the focus of scholars. In this paper, the vibration signals of the OLTC including good condition, tap loosening, tap abrasion and insufficient energy-storage are obtained by simulating experiment. Meanwhile, in order to characterize OLTCs in different conditions, a characteristic parameter Marginal Phase Space Distribution Coefficient (MPPDC) is proposed based on phase space reconstruction technology. Furthermore, based on MPPDC and fuzzy set, a fault diagnosis strategy of OLTC is proposed in this paper. The experimental results show that based on the method proposed in this paper, the fault types of the OLTC can be effectively identified, which provides the theoretical basis for the on-line monitoring technology of OLTC.

data.abstract: Oil-immersed power transformers are essential in power plants, where they ensure voltage regulation and reliable energy distribution. The On-Load Tap Changer (OLTC) is critical for voltage stability but can suffer from faults, such as bouncing contacts, leading to performance degradation and potential failure. This paper explores the use of various diagnostic techniques, including Dynamic Resistance Measurement (DRM), Insulation Resistance Testing, Dissipation Factor Testing, Transformer Turn Ratio Testing, Excitation Current Testing, and Winding Resistance Testing, for condition monitoring and fault detection in power transformers. The focus is on how DRM can effectively detect OLTC bouncing contacts, offering early fault detection and improving predictive maintenance. By integrating these diagnostic methods, power plant operators can enhance transformer reliability and reduce downtime.

data.abstract: On-load Tap-changer (OLTC) is one of the significant components in power transformer. The breakdown of frequently switched OLTC may cause the cutoff of the corresponding in-service transformer. Hence, suitable indicators are needed for effectively monitoring the operation condition of OLTC. Although the vibration analysis method has been proven to be effective for the mechanical condition assessment of the OLTC, the diagnostic parameters are mostly submerged in the noises during the switch-over process of OLTC. To solve this problem, this paper presents a new methodology - resonance-based sparse signal decomposition (RSSD) - to extract the determining vibration signals’ features for the monitoring of OLTC. The vibration signal is decomposed into high-resonance components, low-resonance components, and redundant components. The obtained fault characteristics are mainly contained in the high-resonance components, which can be used for the fault detection.

data.abstract: On-load tap changers (OLTCs) are critical components of power transformers. In recent years, condition monitoring technologies for OLTCs based on vibration signals have attracted increasing research interest. However, practical applications still face several challenges, including background noise interference, insufficient characterization of transient signals, signal complexity, difficulty in detecting subtle anomalies, and ambiguous associations between fault modes and signal features. To address these issues, this paper proposes an OLTC acoustic fingerprint feature recognition method based on multidimensional phase-space trajectory analysis. First, an OLTC fault simulation platform was established, in which typical mechanical faults—such as fastener loosening, contact wear, and insufficient spring energy storage—were physically simulated. Corresponding vibration signals were then acquired under different operating conditions. Considering the independence of vibration characteristics at different locations of the distribution transformer, a blind source separation method based on endpoint detection was employed to separate OLTC vibration signals from the operational noise of the transformer body. Given the nonlinear and chaotic characteristics of OLTC vibration signals, phase-space reconstruction was introduced for signal analysis. Based on the reconstructed phase space, characteristic patterns and geometric feature parameters corresponding to different mechanical states of the OLTC were extracted. Furthermore, a two-dimensional membership function was constructed using the phase-space trajectories, and fuzzy inference based on predefined fuzzy rules was applied to compute representative feature parameters. A feature parameter database was subsequently established to enable OLTC condition identification. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed diagnostic model can effectively classify and identify OLTC fault conditions using vibration signals, achieving an average classification accuracy exceeding 91.25%. The proposed method provides an effective non-intrusive approach for online monitoring and mechanical fault diagnosis of OLTCs without interrupting normal transformer operation.
